g.text: TrialWatch — ADR roadmap for the AI decisions

One session = one decision record (ADR) + the lab that tests it. Session Sn writes docs/adr/ADR-00n-….excalidraw. Card numbers refer to ai-architecture-decisions.excalidraw. As of 2026-11-01: ADR-001 accepted.
Read the card on the map; learn its TERMS.
Write the question in one sentence.
List 2–3 real options. The current proposal is
Compare them against S1's targets: quality,
cost, risk, how hard to undo.
Decide, and write what evidence would change
Do the lab: code that tests the decision.
Mark the ADR accepted; turn the card green on
You write the reasoning. Claude asks, challenges,
explains terms and reviews the lab.
Arrows show the suggested order. NEEDS lists hard
ADR-NNN title · status · date · cards · exam tags
quality · cost · risk · effort · how hard to undo

each session turns one card green.

Confirming the old answer is a good outcome.
No ADR is accepted before its lab has run.
One session, one ADR. Then stop.
Not up for reset: CTIS client, snapshots,
Postgres, compose. Built, tested, not AI.

S1–S14 take one check end to end: the results-document check. The other two checks reuse most of it.
Publication finder (Europe PMC): short ADRs only for search and matching; S15 decides whether it needs an
Outcome-switch detector: a short ADR for the COMPare labels and the comparison rule.
Schema, gateway, review, audit trail, cost and publication policy carry over unchanged.
